practice_description.medium: AI-generated video, deepfake performance, installation, generative imagery
practice_description.practice_summary: Jake Elwes creates artworks using GANs and deepfake technology to explore identity, representation, and the politics of training data, most notably through the Zizi project -- a series of works using deepfake technology trained on drag performers with their full consent and collaboration.
practice_description.methodology: Elwes works closely with drag performers from the London scene, filming them performing and using this footage as training data for GAN and deepfake models. The collaborative process foregrounds consent -- performers are credited, involved in decisions about how their likenesses are used, and the training data itself becomes a subject of the work. Elwes studied fine art at the Slade School (UCL) and has a background in both traditional art and machine learning. His process involves training custom models, curating training datasets as an artistic act, and creating outputs that oscillate between recognizable human forms and abstract machine hallucination.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Elwes' Zizi project directly addresses how training data, consent, and identity intersect in generative systems -- core concerns for any graph-curated exhibition using AI. His work demonstrates how the politics of the dataset IS the artwork, making it essential reference for A(DAI)'s approach to data materiality.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Partially -- the deepfake models and their outputs could function as substrate layers in a larger generative composition. The trained models encode specific identities and performances that could be recombined or recomposed.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Limited direct engagement with graph-based composition, but the Zizi project creates relational networks between performers, their digital doubles, and audiences. The work explores how identity is constructed through relationships between data points.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: Yes -- the generative models produce continuously varying outputs. Zizi: Queering the Dataset creates an infinite generative stream of faces that morph and transform. The real-time installations respond to audience presence and input.

works.title: Zizi: Queering the Dataset
works.description: Video installation using a GAN trained on drag performers' faces to generate an infinite stream of morphing, gender-fluid faces. The work intervenes in biased facial recognition datasets by inserting drag performance into the training data, creating faces that resist binary classification.
works.relevance: Demonstrates how curating training data is a creative and political act. Directly relevant to A(DAI)'s concerns about data provenance, consent, and how knowledge systems encode power.

works.title: The Zizi Show
works.description: A deepfake drag cabaret performed by AI-generated performers, streamed during COVID lockdowns. Real drag performers' movements and voices were transformed through deepfake models in real time, creating a virtual cabaret that questioned liveness, presence, and digital identity.
works.relevance: Explores how AI performance can preserve and transform live culture. Demonstrates real-time generative performance using consented training data from a specific community.

works.title: Zizi & Me
works.description: Interactive installation where visitors stand in front of a screen and see themselves transformed into deepfake drag performers in real time. The work makes the experience of having one's identity transformed by AI viscerally immediate.
works.relevance: Directly engages audiences in the experience of AI identity transformation, making abstract concerns about deepfakes and consent physically tangible. Responsive-to-input modality relevant to Sense Room.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: Elwes does not explicitly design protocols or governance systems as artwork, but his practice implicitly designs consent protocols for AI training data in creative contexts. The collaborative agreements with drag performers, the crediting systems, and the ethical framework around the Zizi project function as informal protocols for consented AI art-making.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: Informal consent and collaboration framework for working with drag performers as AI training data contributors. Not a formal protocol or infrastructure, but a practice-based model for ethical deepfake art.

commons_orientation.licence_model: Unknown -- works are presented in gallery/institutional contexts; the trained models and code are not publicly released as open source [uncertain]
commons_orientation.commons_summary: Elwes' practice is oriented toward community benefit and representation rather than enclosure, but does not explicitly build commons infrastructure. The work gives visibility to drag culture and queer identity within AI art discourse. The training data remains within the artist's practice rather than being released as a shared resource.

governance_model.governance_detail: Elwes is the primary artist and decision-maker, but works collaboratively with drag performers who have input into how their likenesses are used. This is a collaborative solo practice rather than a collective or DAO -- the artist leads but foregrounds consent and performer agency.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Consent is central to the practice. Drag performers are filmed with full knowledge and agreement that their likenesses will be used for AI training. Performers are credited and involved in the process. The consent framework is informal but deeply embedded in the working method -- Elwes has spoken extensively about building trust with the drag community over time.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Primarily solo authorship with acknowledged collaboration. Elwes is credited as the artist, but the drag performers are recognized as essential contributors and collaborators. The AI is treated as a transformative tool rather than a co-author.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: Generative installations produce continuously varying outputs from the trained models. Zizi & Me responds to visitor input in real time. The Zizi Show involved live-streamed performances with real-time deepfake transformation. The underlying models are trained and relatively fixed, but their outputs are generative and variable.

data_materiality.data_sources: Video recordings of London drag performers performing, posing, and moving. Facial imagery and body movement data captured with performers' consent. Standard facial recognition datasets are referenced critically (the work 'queers' existing biased datasets).
data_materiality.data_provenance: Fully consented -- all training data is captured directly from collaborating drag performers who are aware of and agree to the use. The ethical provenance of the data is a core subject of the artwork, contrasting with scraped/unconsented datasets used in commercial AI.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: The GAN-generated faces operate in a latent space where identity features are encoded as continuous vectors. Elwes navigates and interpolates within this latent space to create morphing sequences that move between recognizable faces and abstract hallucination. The latent space becomes a space of gender fluidity and identity transformation.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: Primarily visual (generated video/imagery), with audio components in The Zizi Show (voice, music). Not operating in a unified multimodal embedding space.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Works are typically presented as large-scale video installations in gallery settings. Zizi & Me uses a camera and screen setup for interactive visitor engagement. The Zizi Show was a streamed performance (web/screen modality during COVID). Works occupy gallery space as immersive video environments with projected or screen-based imagery.

interoperability.composability: Limited -- works are self-contained gallery installations. The trained models are not released as tools for others to use. Outputs are video/imagery that could theoretically serve as inputs elsewhere but are not designed for composability.
interoperability.technical_openness: Closed -- models and code are not publicly released. Works are experienced in institutional exhibition contexts. [uncertain]

technical_approach.stack: GANs (StyleGAN and similar architectures) for face generation; deepfake/face-swap neural networks for real-time identity transformation; custom Python/ML pipelines; GPU-based real-time inference for interactive installations; video capture and processing

network_position.scene_affiliation: London AI art scene; Slade School of Fine Art (UCL) network; UK digital arts institutions (Barbican, Science Gallery London, arebyte); AI ethics and art discourse; LGBTQ+ art and drag culture; European media art (Ars Electronica)
network_position.connections: Holly Herndon / Mat Dryhurst (shared discourse on consent and AI training data); Spawning AI (consent infrastructure relevant to his practice); Hito Steyerl (shared concerns about AI and representation); Serpentine Arts Technologies; broader UK AI art community

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Elwes brings deep practical experience with consented AI training data from specific communities. His work on identity, drag culture, and the politics of datasets would enrich A(DAI)'s discourse on data provenance, consent, and representation. Could serve as a case study for ethical deepfake practice and community-engaged AI art-making.
